questions.q: What are the three pieces this lesson says you combine to build your first real model?
options: A dbt Cloud account, a Snowflake trial, and a GitHub repo
A Python script, a YAML file, and a Docker container
A declared source, a staging model built on it, and ref() calls connecting them
Three separate staging models with no other logic
questions.explain: This lesson walks through combining a source, its staging model, and ref() calls into one new downstream model.

questions.q: After writing a new model .sql file, what extra step is required to register it with the project?
options: None — dbt discovers any .sql file under a configured model-path automatically
Running a separate `dbt register` command
Emailing dbt Labs to add it to the catalog
Adding its filename manually to dbt_project.yml
questions.explain: There is no registration step — dbt automatically discovers any .sql file located under a configured model-path.

questions.q: In the real terminal screenshot in this lesson, what changed in the `dbt run` output after the user added their new customers model?
options: It now reports 'Found 3 models' instead of 2, and builds the new model alongside the starter ones
It reported an unrecoverable error and refused to run
Nothing changed — the new model was silently ignored
The starter models were deleted automatically
questions.explain: The screenshot shows dbt finding 3 models instead of 2 and successfully building the newly added customers model.

questions.q: If a new model file doesn't show up in a run, what two things does this lesson say to check first?
options: Whether the Snowflake warehouse is large enough
Whether the file has been committed to Git
Whether dbt Cloud's subscription has been renewed
Whether the file is under a configured model-path and whether it has a .sql extension
questions.explain: Only two things make a file 'a model' to dbt: living under a configured model-path, and having a .sql extension.

questions.q: How can you build just one specific model instead of the whole project?
options: dbt run --only-one
dbt run --select <model_name>
You must delete every other model file first
There is no way to run a single model
questions.explain: The --select flag lets you target a single model (or a set of models) instead of running the entire project.
